newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish FinMin spokeswoman dismisses EMU report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish FinMin spokeswoman dismisses EMU report.

text.p: A spokeswoman for the Swedish finance minister dismissed on Wednesday as speculation a radio report saying the finance and prime minister did not want to join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) during the mandate period 1998-2002 without new elections being held.
"This report is only speculation," a spokeswoman for Finance Minister Erik Asbrink told Reuters.
The spokeswoman added that Asbrink said it had not been decided when the ruling Social Democrats would announce their view on EMU membership.

The public radio news report said that according to its sources Asbrink and Prime Minister Goran Persson had agreed that the government could say no to EMU now and join during the next mandate period without new parliamentary elections being held.

"This means that there will either be new elections or that Sweden cannot be a member of EMU until 2003 after scheduled parliamentary elections in 2002 -- if Persson and Asbrink get to decide," the news programme Ekot said.
The heads of the Social Democratic party are expected to announce their EMU view on Friday, the radio report said.
